manufacturing_considerations.reason: Process hints are an extractor interpretation, not geometry. Mode I receives no such hints, so the Mode II prompt builder strips this section to keep the comparison about the INPUT REPRESENTATION (drawing vs CAD facts). Kept here for the human G2 process gate.

items.text: Recessed levels face both directions (up-facing below the top and down-facing above the bottom): at least two setups (flip about a horizontal axis) are needed, or the down-facing faces stay unmachined.
items.label: GEOMETRICALLY_INFERRED

items.text: M-WINDOW-01: smallest concave corner R8 -> finishing cutter diameter <= 16 mm (smaller to avoid full-radius engagement).
items.label: GEOMETRICALLY_INFERRED
items.basis: min concave radius of the section loop

items.text: M-KEYWAY-01: slot width 8 mm -> cutter diameter <= that width; the slot's square closed end cannot be made exactly by a rotating cutter (corner radius = cutter radius) unless broached/slotted.
items.label: GEOMETRICALLY_INFERRED

items.text: M-PINS-01: the pins stand above the boss top, so the boss top must be machined AROUND them (contour each pin); the raw stock top must lie at or above the pin tops.
items.label: GEOMETRICALLY_INFERRED

items.text: M-FILLET-01: R2 fillets between horizontal and vertical faces need a ball/bull-nose cutter or are left as a documented simulator limitation.
items.label: GEOMETRICALLY_INFERRED

limitations: Only tool axes parallel to a world axis are analysed (true for the current model); an inclined axis is reported as an error, not guessed.

Feature types (hole, bore with slot, window, pin, boss) are inferred from topology and geometry; the B-rep carries no manufacturing semantics (no tolerances, fits, surface finish, material, thread callouts). Those stay UNKNOWN unless a human annotation supplies them.
Face 'orientation' is an undocumented Onshape field; its meaning is an observed convention.

Curved edges are represented by their start, quarter, mid and end points when mapped to a face's parameter space; sections are exact for vertical side edges and approximate (piecewise linear) where a side edge is a blend curve. Slices are taken at band mid-heights, away from the R2 blends.
Blends (tori) are reported separately as fillets and are not part of the section loops.
Contour elements are CAD geometry, not toolpaths: entry points, direction, step-downs and cutter compensation are process decisions for the AI proposal and the human gates.
